context_rule: Classify only the current request; use the session context, if given, only to interpret it. A follow-up that approves or continues a plan proposed earlier (for example '진행', '응 만들어줘', '둘 다 반영') has the role and effort of the work that plan describes.

role.instructions: Which single role best describes the main deliverable of the current request? Judge the requested output, not keywords in the text.${context_rule}

criteria.implementation: Add new behavior or a feature.
criteria.fix: Repair a bug or failure in existing behavior.
criteria.lint: Fix only spelling, typos, formatting, style, or static-analysis issues such as unused imports.
criteria.test: Writing, changing, or running tests is the main goal.
criteria.plan: Produce a plan for work before executing it.
criteria.design: A structure, interface, or architecture proposal is the requested deliverable.
criteria.review: Inspect existing changes or code and report findings without modifying them.
criteria.analysis: Explain causes or behavior, or answer in chat only (translation, wording, naming, or a short message) without implementing or editing project files.

effort.instructions: Choose the reasoning effort from how hard the decisions are, not from how much code must be read. Judge it independently of role, file count, or keywords: planning or reviewing a change needs the same effort as making it.${context_rule}

criteria.low: One function, option, or explanation is involved and the request states or clearly implies the approach, even if that code must be read first.
criteria.medium: Existing parts are connected or changed by established patterns, edge cases need judgment, or missing details must be gathered before deciding.
criteria.high: Correctness depends on interacting guarantees such as concurrency, consistency, compatibility, or security, or real design tradeoffs or uncertain diagnosis remain.
criteria.xhigh: Rare timing-dependent failures across several subsystems, or changes where a mistake would corrupt or lose production data, bypass security, or cause irreversible harm.
criteria.max: The broadest and most demanding reasoning is needed: several interacting systems, substantial uncertainty, and high consequences require sustained analysis beyond xhigh.

tier.instructions: Which model intelligence tier does this request need, considering task complexity, context scope, domain knowledge, and precision? Judge the required model capability independently of reasoning effort: more reasoning effort cannot supply domain or API knowledge a model lacks. Judge what the task actually requires, not domain words. A product or tool name in the request or session context is not evidence by itself; decide from what the deliverable must do.${context_rule}

criteria.economy: Self-contained or localized tasks (e.g., single function/class/module implementation, targeted bug fixes, tests, refactoring, or straightforward routines) that use general-purpose code or widely used frameworks in common ways and whose result tests or values stated in the request can confirm; capable fast economy models (e.g., Luna, Haiku 5.5, Flash) handle these well when given appropriate reasoning effort. Mentioning a 3D tool, game engine, or graphics product does not make a task frontier: in such a project, work that touches only general-purpose code or files (packaging, build or CI scripts, file handling, log parsing, docs, changelogs, config, tests of plain helpers), a commit or test run, changing a stated value, name, or typo, or a question about a well-known feature or concept stays economy.
criteria.balanced: Multi-module or cross-component feature work, complex interactions between subsystems, non-trivial state management, or architecture-guided changes requiring balanced model capability (e.g., Terra, Sonnet 5.5).
criteria.frontier: System-wide architectural design, subtle cross-system reasoning, mission-critical concurrency/security/data-loss guarantees, or deep foundational decisions. Also frontier, at any size, a task that needs any one of: (1) code that drives a 3D/DCC tool's, game engine's, or graphics API's own scripting interface (e.g., building meshes, materials, node trees, operators, or UI panels through that API), or writing or debugging shader logic; (2) spatial or geometric math done right (e.g., intersection tests, coordinate spaces, transforms, rotations, projection, lighting); (3) diagnosing or fixing rendered output that tests cannot check (e.g., depth precision, shading, sorting, or normal artifacts). A stated value, name, or typo change stays economy even inside such code. These require frontier model capability (e.g., Sol, Opus 5.5, Argon).

target.instructions: Which outcome does the current request ask for? Judge the requested outcome, not keywords. Active-project metadata only supplies an omitted subject. An acknowledgement or approval is route only when it authorizes an executable proposal in session context.${context_rule}

criteria.route: The user asks for an outcome in the active project or its work: investigate, analyze or explain status or behavior, implement, fix, test, lint, plan, design, or review. A follow-up authorizing an executable proposal in session context is route.
criteria.no_route: Chit-chat or an acknowledgement or approval without an executable proposal in session context, or a request explicitly unrelated to software development.
